speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties; to begin my assessment, have you noticed if these symptoms are getting worse over a few weeks, months, or years?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis)

The combination of progressive bulbar symptoms (speech slurring), sphincter dysfunction (incontinence), and significant motor weakness (requiring a wheelchair) over 3-4 months is highly concerning for a motor neuron disease. I am requesting a MRI of the brain and cervical spine, as well as blood work to rule out other metabolic or structural causes.
